'''Michael Elliott''', {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|CBE|FRS|FRSC}} (30 September 1924 – 17 October 2007) was a [[chemist]] and Lawes Trust Senior [[Fellow]] at [[Rothamsted Research|Rothamsted Experimental Station]] who invented and commercialised the development of novel [[insecticide]]s known as [[pyrethroid]]s.<ref name=ElliottJanes1978>{{cite journal|last1=Elliott|first1=M.|last2=Janes|first2=N. F.|title=Synthetic pyrethroids? A new class of insecticide|journal=[[Chemical Society Reviews]]|volume=7|issue=4|year=1978|pages=473|doi=10.1039/cs9780700473}}</ref><ref name=ElliottFarnham1967>{{cite journal|last1=Elliott|first1=M.|last2=Farnham|first2=A. W.|last3=Janes|first3=N. F.|last4=Needham|first4=P. H.|last5=Pearson|first5=B. C.|title=5-Benzyl-3-furylmethyl Chrysanthemate: a New Potent Insecticide|journal=Nature|volume=213|issue=5075|year=1967|pages=493–494|doi=10.1038/213493a0|bibcode=1967Natur.213..493E|s2cid=4255634}}</ref><ref name=ElliottFarnham1973>{{cite journal|last1=Elliott|first1=M.|last2=Farnham|first2=A. W.|last3=Janes|first3=N. F.|last4=Needham|first4=P. H.|last5=Pulman|first5=D. A.|last6=Stevenson|first6=J. H.|title=A Photostable Pyrethroid|journal=Nature|volume=246|issue=5429|year=1973|pages=169–170|doi=10.1038/246169a0|pmid=4586114|bibcode=1973Natur.246..169E|s2cid=4176154}}</ref><ref name="ElliottFarnham1974b">{{cite journal|last1=Elliott|first1=M.|last2=Farnham|first2=A. W.|last3=Janes|first3=N. F.|last4=Needham|first4=P. H.|last5=Pulman|first5=D. A.|title=Synthetic insecticide with a new order of activity|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=248|issue=5450|year=1974|pages=710–711|pmid=4833277|doi=10.1038/248710a0|bibcode=1974Natur.248..710E|s2cid=4150273}}</ref>

==Education==
Elliott was educated at [[The Skinners' School]] in [[Tunbridge Wells]] and the [[University of Southampton]] where he was awarded [[Bachelor of Science]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degrees.{{when|date=August 2016}}<ref name=whowaswho/>

==Research and career==
Elliott led the team that invented the major pyrethroid insecticides [[Resmethrin|bioresmethrin]], [[permethrin]], [[cypermethrin]] and [[deltamethrin]].<ref name=rsbm>{{cite journal|last1=Pickett|first1=John|authorlink=John A. Pickett|title=Michael Elliott CBE. 30 September 1924 — 17 October 2007|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|volume=62|pages=109–123|year=2016|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2016.0018|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=guardian>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306111655/http://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/dec/05/guardianobituaries.obituaries1|archivedate=2016-03-06|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/dec/05/guardianobituaries.obituaries1|title=Obituary: Michael Elliott, Chemist whose research led to modern insecticides|website=[[The Guardian]]|location=London|first=Andrew|last= Farnham|year=2007}}</ref> In 2009 it was estimated that pyrethroid-treated [[mosquito net]]s significantly decreased the number of deaths due to [[malaria]].<ref name=rsbm/>

==Awards and honours==
Elliott was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1979|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1979]]<ref name=rsbm/> and appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in 1982.<ref name=whowaswho>{{Who's Who | title=ELLIOTT, Dr Michael | id = U14856 | volume = 2016 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford|type=was}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] in 1989.
